first.rationale: Northwind faces concurrent pressure: competitor pricing erosion in SMB segment, 6% activation decline, and 4% onboarding completion decline. Memory 73 demonstrates targeted promotional pricing drives strong acquisition and revenue lift in price-sensitive SMB segments while accelerating time-to-first-value. This directly addresses the competitive threat and supports activation recovery through faster onboarding impact. Memory 31 (signup simplification) is verified to validate whether activation decline is driven by friction vs. messaging. Memory 73 verification confirms the pricing mechanism still performs and informs segment targeting. Promotional pricing targets the immediate revenue risk (competitor acquisition), aligns with proven memory, and can be deployed at standard scale within one week. Referral incentive (memory_57) suits revenue growth in established segments but doesn't address activation decline or competitive acquisition pressure. Activation messaging (memory_91) is secondary—if onboarding friction or pricing is the blocker, messaging alone won't recover the 6% activation shortfall. Enterprise sales assist is orthogonal to the SMB-driven crisis. Preserving uncertainty: scale remains standard rather than broad rollout, allowing measured validation of whether pricing intervention recovers activation when paired with faster onboarding.
